1. The petitioner is before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C. No.624/2021 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 323, 504, 506 read with Section 149 OF IPC.
2.

Heard the learned counsel Shri Vijay S.Chiniwar appearing for the petitioner; learned HCGP Shri V.S. Kalasurmath appearing for respondent No.1; & learned counsel Shri Santosh Nargund appearing for respondent No.2.
3. The petitioner is the accused No.5.
The 2nd respondent is the complainant-wife of accused No.1.
Accused No.1 and the complainant get married on NC: 2023:KHC-D:9045 08.07.2018.
From the wedlock, the couple have a child as well.
It transpires that after the birth of the child, the relationship between the husband and wife flounders and the complainant seeks to register a complaint for afore quoted offences on 03.02.2021.
The Police after investigation file a charge sheet against all the accused, the petitioner is accused No.5 in C.C. No.624/2021.
Filing of the charge sheet is what drives the petitioner to this Court in the subject petition.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the he is the friend of accused No.1 - husband and has nothing to do with the dispute between the husband and the wife and is dragged into these proceedings without the rhyme or reason.
Learned counsel would seek quashment of the entire proceeding.

5. Learned HCGP taking this Court through the documents appended to the petition with particular Ashpak S/O Davalsab Budihal vs The State Of Karnataka on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115845649/
2 reference to the charge sheet as obtaining the column No.17 would seek to contend that the allegation against the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9045 petitioner would meet the ingredients of Section 323 of the IPC.

6. Learned counsel representing the complainant would toe the lines of the learned HCGP.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and have perused the material available on record.
8. The relationship between accused No.1 and the complainant is not in dispute.
The petitioner being the friend of accused No.1 - husband is also not in dispute.
On the relationship of the petitioner or the complainant and the husband turning sour, complaint comes to be registered by the wife.
A perusal at the complaint would indicate sprinkling offences against the petitioner.
The Police after registration of crime conduct investigation.
The investigation leads to filing of a final report / the charge sheet against the petitioner including others.
The charge NC: 2023:KHC-D:9045 sheet as obtaining in column No.17 insofar as it concerns the petitioner, reads as follows:
Except the aforesaid finding against the petitioner, there is no other offence alleged.

No other offences can be alleged against the petitioner as the other offence is Section 498A of the IPC, the petitioner is the friend of accused No.1 - husband, who cannot be construed to be a member of the family as is necessary under Section 498-A of the IPC.
A friend cannot be thus hauled into the web of crime in an offence under Section 498A of the IPC.
What remains is Section 323 of the IPC.
To meet the offence under Section 323 of the IPC, the ingredients of are found in the portion quoted at column No.17.
Therefore, the petition deserves to be allowed insofar as it concerns the offence under Section 498A of the IPC.
Insofar as the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9045 other offences are concerned, the charge sheet meeting its ingredients, I deem it appropriate to reject the petition insofar as the other offences are concerned.

For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed in part.
